title: nf-core/ampliseq pipeline parameters
description: Amplicon sequencing analysis workflow using DADA2 and QIIME2

input.help_text:
Path to sample sheet, either tab-separated (.tsv), comma-separated (.csv), or in YAML format (.yml/.yaml), that points to compressed fastq files.

The sample sheet must have at least two entries:
- required: `sample`, `fastq_1`
- optional: `fastq_2`, `run`, `control`, `quant_reading`

Sample IDs must start with a letter and can only contain letters, numbers or underscores.

Related parameters are:
- `--sequencing_type` to define the data type (default expected: paired-end Illumina data)
- Choose an appropriate reference taxonomy for the type of amplicon (16S/18S/ITS/CO1) (default: DADA2 assignTaxonomy and 16S rRNA sequence database)

input_fasta.help_text:
Path to fasta format file with sequences that will be taxonomically classified. The fasta file input option can be used to taxonomically classify previously produced ASV/OTU sequences.

The fasta sequence header line may contain a description, that will be kept as part of the sequence name. However, tabs will be changed into spaces.

Related parameters are:
- Choose an appropriate reference taxonomy for the type of amplicon (16S/18S/ITS/CO1) (default: DADA2 assignTaxonomy and 16S rRNA sequence database)

metadata.description: Path to metadata sheet, when missing most downstream analysis are skipped (barplots, PCoA plots, ...).
metadata.help_text:
This is optional, but for performing downstream analysis such as barplots, diversity indices or differential abundance testing, a metadata file is essential.

Related parameter:
- `--metadata_category` (optional) to choose columns that are used for testing significance

For example:

```bash
--metadata "path/to/metadata.tsv"
```

The first column in the tab-separated metadata file is the sample identifier column (required header: `ID`) and defines the sample or feature IDs associated with your study. More details are in the usage documentation.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

primer_fwd.help_text:
In amplicon sequencing methods, PCR with specific primers produces the amplicon of interest. These primer sequences need to be trimmed from the reads before further processing and are also required for producing an appropriate classifier. Do not use here any technical sequence such as adapter sequences but only the primer sequence that matches the biological amplicon.

For example:

```bash
--primer_fwd "GTGYCAGCMGCCGCGGTAA" --primer_rev "GGACTACNVGGGTWTCTAAT"
```

primer_rev.help_text:
In amplicon sequencing methods, PCR with specific primers produces the amplicon of interest. These primer sequences need to be trimmed from the reads before further processing and are also required for producing an appropriate classifier. Do not use here any technical sequence such as adapter sequences but only the primer sequence that matches the biological amplicon.

For example:

```bash
--primer_fwd GTGYCAGCMGCCGCGGTAA --primer_rev GGACTACNVGGGTWTCTAAT
```

sample_inference.help_text: If samples are treated independent (lowest sensitivity and lowest resources), pooled (highest sensitivity and resources) or [only for DADA2] pseudo-pooled (balance between required resources and sensitivity).

max_len_asv.help_text: Remove ASV that are above the maximum length threshold (default: filter is disabled, otherwise 1000000). Lowering the threshold might reduce false positive ASVs (e.g. PCR off-targets).

dada_ref_taxonomy.help_text:
Choose any of the supported databases, and optionally also specify the version. Database and version are separated by an equal sign (`=`, e.g. `silva=138`). This will download the desired database, format it to produce a file that is compatible with DADA2's assignTaxonomy and another file that is compatible with DADA2's addSpecies.

Database keys are given in **lower case**; the values in parentheses below are the exact strings `--dada_ref_taxonomy` accepts for that database (the unversioned key selects the most recent/default version).

**SSU rRNA**
- SBDI-GTDB, a Sativa-vetted version of the GTDB 16S rRNA, the default (`sbdi-gtdb`, `sbdi-gtdb=R11-RS232-1`, `sbdi-gtdb=R10-RS226-2`, `sbdi-gtdb=R09-RS220-2`, `sbdi-gtdb=R09-RS220-1`, `sbdi-gtdb=R08-RS214-1`, `sbdi-gtdb=R07-RS207-1`, `sbdi-gtdb=R06-RS202-3`, `sbdi-gtdb=R06-RS202-1`)
- SILVA ribosomal RNA gene database project, 16S rRNA (`silva`, `silva=144`, `silva=138.2`, `silva=138`, `silva=132`)
- GTDB - Genome Taxonomy Database, 16S rRNA (`gtdb`, `gtdb=R11-RS232`, `gtdb=R10-RS226`, `gtdb=R09-RS220`, `gtdb=R08-RS214`, `gtdb=R07-RS207`, `gtdb=R06-RS202`, `gtdb=R05-RS95`)
- RDP - Ribosomal Database Project, 16S rRNA (`rdp`, `rdp=18`)
- Greengenes2, 16S rRNA (`greengenes2`, `greengenes2=2024.09`)
- PR2 - Protist Reference Ribosomal Database, 18S rRNA (Note: also contains plastid/chloroplast 16S rRNA sequences) (`pr2`, `pr2=5.1.0`, `pr2=5.0.0`, `pr2=4.14.0`, `pr2=4.13.0`)

**ITS** (also rRNA, listed next to SSU rRNA)
- UNITE - eukaryotic nuclear ribosomal ITS region: fungi only (`unite-fungi`, `unite-fungi=10.0`, `unite-fungi=9.0`, `unite-fungi=8.3`, `unite-fungi=8.2`), or all eukaryotes (`unite-alleuk`, `unite-alleuk=10.0`, `unite-alleuk=9.0`, `unite-alleuk=8.3`, `unite-alleuk=8.2`)
- GloSED - Global Standardised Soil Eukaryome Dataset, fungal ITS; SH support not available (`glosed`, `glosed=1.0.0`)

**COI**
- COIDB - eukaryotic Cytochrome Oxidase I (COI) from The Barcode of Life Data System (BOLD) (`coidb`, `coidb=221216`)
- MIDORI2-CO1 (`midori2-co1`, `midori2-co1=gb250`)

**nifH**
- Zehr-nifH (`zehr-nifh`, `zehr-nifh=2.5.0`)

Several comma-separated databases may be given (e.g. `sbdi-gtdb,silva`) to run DADA2 taxonomic classification against each of them; one full set of output files is published per listed database. By default, only the **first-listed** database feeds every downstream step that expects a single taxonomy (QIIME2 filtering, diversity, barplots, ANCOM, R objects); use `--consolidate_taxonomies` to instead pick a per-ASV winner across all listed databases.

Please note that commercial/non-academic entities [require licensing](https://www.arb-silva.de/silva-license-information) for SILVA v132 (non-default) but not from v138 on (default). This list (including the exact accepted database/version strings) always matches `conf/ref_databases.config` -- supply an invalid value (e.g. `x`) to have the pipeline print the current list. See also the [usage docs](https://nf-co.re/ampliseq/docs/usage/#taxonomic-classification).
dada_ref_taxonomy.description: Name of supported database(s), and optionally also version number(s) -- comma-separated for multiple databases

cut_dada_ref_taxonomy.help_text: Expected amplified sequences are extracted from the DADA2 reference taxonomy using the primer sequences, that might improve classification. This is not applied to species classification (assignSpecies) but only for lower taxonomic levels (assignTaxonomy).
cut_dada_ref_taxonomy.description: If the expected amplified sequences are extracted from the DADA2 reference taxonomy database

qiime_ref_taxonomy.help_text:
Choose any of the supported databases, and optionally also specify the version. Database and version are separated by an equal sign (`=`, e.g. `silva=138`) . This will download the desired database and initiate taxonomic classification with QIIME2 and the chosen database.

If both, `--dada_ref_taxonomy` and `--qiime_ref_taxonomy` are used, DADA2 classification will be used for downstream analysis.

The following databases are supported:
- SILVA ribosomal RNA gene database project - 16S rRNA
- UNITE - eukaryotic nuclear ribosomal ITS region - ITS
- Greengenes (only testing!)

Generally, using `silva`, `unite-fungi`, or `unite-alleuk` will select the most recent supported version. For testing purposes, the tiny database `greengenes85` (dereplicated at 85% sequence similarity) is available. For details on what values are valid, please either use an invalid value such as `x` (causing the pipeline to send an error message with all valid values) or see `conf/ref_databases.config`.
qiime_ref_taxonomy.description: Name of supported database, and optionally also version number
